papers.title: The DYNAM-O Toolbox: Characterizing Individualized Neural Signatures in Sleep EEG.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Introduced the DYNAM-O Toolbox, an open-source pipeline for data-driven characterization of individualized transient oscillations in sleep EEG using a multi-resolution time-frequency peak detection approach. In 112 adults, it replicated higher fast-spindle frequency in females and identified greater low-alpha transient oscillatory activity in females as a novel sex difference.

papers.title: Assessing accelerometry as an alternative to electromyography for mouse sleep scoring
papers.summary: Systematically compared accelerometry (Acc) against electromyography (EMG) for manual sleep scoring in mice using hippocampal LFP. Epoch-by-epoch agreement exceeded 90% (kappa > 0.8), but Acc underclassified Wake by 4.92% and overclassified NREM sleep by 3.29%, with disagreements reflecting genuine signal differences.

papers.title: Wearable Sleep-Stage Classification: A Systematic Analysis of Signal Modalities, Representations, and Multimodal Fusion.
papers.summary: Systematically analyzed signal modality, representation, and fusion effects on subject-independent wearable sleep staging using DREAMT and MESA cohorts. STFT representations outperformed handcrafted features (e.g., five-class Macro-F1 0.4376 vs 0.3366), BVP was the strongest individual modality, and simple concatenation fusion achieved the best performance without gains from more complex strategies.

papers.title: A context-aware temporal modeling through unified multi-scale temporal encoding and hierarchical sequence learning for single-channel EEG sleep staging.
papers.summary: The paper proposes TempoSleep, a context-aware framework for single-channel EEG sleep staging that combines multi-scale feature extraction and temporal modeling with class-weighted loss and data augmentation. It achieves 89.72% overall accuracy, 85.46% macro F1, and 61.7% F1 for the N1 stage on SleepEDF datasets.

papers.title: Repeated morphine reorganizes sleep-wake states, cortical and central medial thalamic oscillations, and network synchronization in mice.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Investigated how repeated morphine exposure reorganizes sleep-wake states and thalamocortical network oscillations in mice using cortical EEG, central medial thalamic LFP, and EMG. Morphine produced wake promotion, NREM suppression, complete REM loss, and divergent cortical versus thalamic spectral changes, with corticocortical alpha and thalamocortical theta synchronization reduced; abstinence normalized sleep architecture but not spectral abnormalities.

papers.title: Model validation in machine learning: A scenario-based guide from hold-out splits to nested group cross-validation in biomedical and applied research
papers.summary: This tutorial reviews model validation schemes for machine learning, from hold-out splits to nested group cross-validation, linking general principles to biomedical data such as EEG epochs, OCT images, repeated clinical measurements, and multicenter datasets. Using eight controlled scenarios and provided MATLAB/scikit-learn templates, it shows that no validation method is universally best and that the independent unit and all data-dependent operations must match the intended deployment target to avoid leakage and optimistic performance estimates.

papers.title: [Microstructural characteristics of sleep electroencephalogram in obstructive sleep apnea].
papers.journal: Zhonghua er bi yan hou tou jing wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of otorhinolaryngology head and neck surgery
papers.summary: In a case-control study of 1,821 suspected OSA patients, the authors analyzed sleep EEG microstructural features and found that OSA patients showed increased power spectral density across multiple frequency bands, higher slow oscillation density/duration/amplitude during N3, and lower sleep spindle density during N2, with these alterations correlating with OSA severity. The findings suggest cortical hyperarousal and thalamocortical rhythm dysregulation that intensify with disease severity.

papers.title: SleepMambaNet: a lightweight multimodal framework for sleep staging and sleep disorder screening with multicenter validation.
papers.summary: Developed SleepMambaNet, a lightweight multimodal framework combining efficient channel attention and bidirectional Mamba modules for automated sleep staging and exploratory sleep-disorder screening. Validated on ISRUC and a multicenter clinical cohort, it achieved 0.854 accuracy, 0.819 macro-F1, and 0.806 kappa on combined data, and 0.892 accuracy for screening, using only 0.47 million parameters.

papers.title: Suppression of corticospinal excitability by sleep spindles without increase in GABAergic inhibition.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using real-time EEG-triggered paired-pulse TMS during NREM sleep, this study found that corticospinal excitability was strongly reduced in spindle-free N2/N3 sleep and further suppressed during sleep spindles, but contrary to the hypothesis, GABA-A receptor-mediated short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI) was not significantly modulated by spindle presence or phase. Preliminary evidence indicated that co-occurring slow oscillations increased excitability and reduced SICI regardless of spindles.

papers.title: Resting-EEG Characteristics and Classification Model Exploration for Tap Test Prediction in Communicating Hydrocephalus: A Small-Sample Pilot Study.
papers.summary: This small-sample pilot study used resting-state EEG to predict tap test responsiveness in 30 communicating hydrocephalus patients, finding that responders had higher alpha-band power correlating with CRS-R improvement, and that linear machine learning models achieved high AUCs (e.g., 0.982 in the DOC subgroup) comparable to deep learning. The results indicate that EEG spectral features contain linearly separable information for tap test prediction.

papers.title: Data-Efficient EEG-Based Person Identification via Time-Interval-Based Multi-Positive Contrastive Learning.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a data-efficient EEG-based person identification framework using time-interval-based multi-positive contrastive learning (TIB-MPCL), which constructs overlapping, adjacent, and non-adjacent positive samples to exploit temporal diversity. On the PhysioNet dataset, it achieved 99.05% average accuracy with all training samples and 83.86% with only 10 one-second samples per subject; cross-session testing on SEED-IV yielded 83.79% average accuracy.

papers.title: A Deep Neural Network for Predicting Continuous Human EEG Across the Auditory Pathway in Response to Sound.
papers.summary: The authors developed a causal deep neural network foundation model that maps binaural acoustic waveforms directly to high-sample-rate EEG, trained on about 250 hours of EEG from 92 subjects across various stimuli. The model reproduced established auditory brainstem response and temporal response function patterns, with model-grand-average correlations within subject-level human distributions, and closely matched literature values for the binaural interaction component.

papers.title: Bayesian Feature Extraction using Gaussian and Diffused-gamma Priors for High Dimensional Spatio-Temporal Data.
papers.summary: The paper develops a Bayesian feature-extraction framework using Gaussian and Diffused-gamma priors for high-dimensional spatio-temporal data, with posterior computation via MCMC and a two-stage selection procedure. Applied to a multi-subject EEG case study on chronic alcohol exposure, the method improved recovery of sparse features and interpretability in the presence of spatio-temporal dependence.

papers.title: Static and Dynamic Resting-State fMRI Connectivity Show Frequency-Resolved Associations With Intracranial EEG Connectivity.
papers.summary: Using simultaneous intracranial EEG-fMRI recordings from 48 adults with focal epilepsy, this study examined frequency-resolved associations between electrophysiological connectivity and static/dynamic fMRI connectivity. It found robust associations between time-averaged icEEG connectivity and static fMRI connectivity, and window-level dynamic fMRI connectivity was positively associated with icEEG connectivity fluctuations in alpha, beta, and low-gamma bands.

papers.title: Pre-sleep acute stress modulates sleep-dependent emotional memory.
papers.summary: This experimental study examined how acute pre-sleep stress affects overnight consolidation of emotional and neutral memories in 34 healthy adults. Pre-sleep stress was associated with longer slow-wave sleep, elevated high-frequency EEG power, and lower slow oscillation-spindle coupling; memory retention was comparable between groups, but stress altered the relationship between NREM low-frequency power and memory retention, with effects driven by emotional material, and higher evening cortisol independently predicted enhanced emotional memory retention.

papers.title: A High-Density EEG Dataset for Stimulus-Driven Auditory Attention
papers.summary: This paper introduces a high-density EEG dataset and computational framework for instruction-free stimulus-driven auditory attention, integrating stimulus-derived sound priority with trial-specific neural evidence. Behavioral modeling showed that sound priority estimated from previous competitions generalized to unseen pairings, raising held-out prediction AUC from 0.577 to 0.718, while EEG revealed mid-to-late centro-temporal lateralization predictive beyond acoustic asymmetry, supporting an interaction between generalizable stimulus priority and trial-specific neural variability.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Modeling of Directed Transfer Entropy Connectivity for EEG-Based ADHD Classification in Children.
papers.summary: The paper proposes CTE-Net, a Transformer-based deep-learning architecture for EEG-based ADHD classification in children that combines global contextualization with differentiable directed Transfer Entropy connectivity estimation. Evaluated on 120 pediatric participants, CTE-Net achieved window-level accuracy of 80.9±1.7% and participant-level accuracy of 83.4% with ROC-AUC of 90.2%, while the directed Transfer Entropy representation reduced within-subject dispersion by a median of 38.35% relative to raw EEG.

papers.title: Brain-wide reconfiguration of burst firing by psilocybin reveals 5-HT2A-dependent circuit dynamics.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The study used simultaneous multi-region Neuropixels recordings of 46,360 single units from 35 mice, along with EEG, pupillometry, and locomotion monitoring, to characterize psilocybin's acute effects on brain-wide circuit dynamics. Psilocybin selectively reconfigured burst coding rather than mean firing rate across cortical, thalamic, and hippocampal circuits, with most burst effects abolished by the 5-HT2A antagonist ketanserin.

papers.title: Regional and network patterns of sleep-depth-associated brain diffusion changes: an EEG-informed multishell diffusion MRI study.
papers.summary: Combined EEG with repeated multishell diffusion MRI during zolpidem-facilitated sleep in healthy adults to examine sleep-depth-associated diffusion changes. Deeper sleep was linked to lower white-matter anisotropy and lower gray-matter diffusivities, localized to frontocentral sensorimotor and medial frontal-cingulate regions, with seven interregional correlation-network changes sensitive to sleep depth.

papers.title: Effects of visual stimulation on local field potentials in the midbrain medial longitudinal fasciculus nucleus of Cyprinus carpio.
papers.summary: Recorded local field potentials from the bilateral midbrain medial longitudinal fasciculus nucleus (Nflm) of common carp during unilateral visual stimulation that elicited tail movements. Unilateral stimulation increased relative power in theta through high-gamma bands in the contralateral Nflm and reduced sample entropy, supporting a role for Nflm in visual signal processing and carp robot control.

papers.title: Common Electrophysiology Biomarkers Collected at Home Robustly Track Depression Recovery With Deep Brain Stimulation
papers.summary: The study developed an at-home subcallosal cingulate cortex (SCC) LFP data collection platform for ten participants with treatment-resistant depression receiving deep brain stimulation (DBS), testing whether a previously reported electrophysiological biomarker of stable recovery generalizes across cohorts and devices without retraining. The biomarker was found to be robust to confounds such as time of day and stimulation status, showed symptom specificity and stability, and its changes related to pre-DBS white matter structure and network function.

papers.title: Altered EEG-derived functional brain states in Parkinson's disease with mild cognitive impairment.
papers.summary: Applied Leading Eigenvector Dynamics Analysis to source-reconstructed EEG to characterize brain state dynamics in Parkinson's disease with and without mild cognitive impairment. MCI was associated with increased occupancy and duration in state B and reduced engagement and transitions into state D, with state D temporal expression and kinetic accessibility positively correlated with Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores.

papers.title: Task-Oriented Semantic Feature Transmission for Robust EEG Motor Imagery Decoding Under Additive White Gaussian Noise.
papers.summary: The paper evaluated task-oriented residual refinement of filter bank common spatial pattern (FBCSP) features compressed by PCA for four-class motor imagery EEG decoding under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) without increasing transmitted dimension. At K=32, the proposed method achieved 41.10%, 49.46%, and 56.15% balanced accuracy at -10, -5, and 0 dB, respectively, with ten of 24 comparisons significantly better than conventional FBCSP-PCA transmission after correction.

papers.title: Shared EEG functional connectivity patterns between time reproduction and working memory.
papers.summary: The study analyzed shared EEG functional connectivity patterns during an intervallic time reproduction (TR) task and an n-back working memory (WM) task in 52 participants. It found a positive correlation between WM capacity and TR precision, overlapping networks between tasks, and no sex differences in performance or connectivity.

papers.title: Redundant Perceptual Inputs Modulate Early Neural Activity Patterns in Visual Working Memory: Evidence from EEG Decoding.
papers.summary: The study applied multivariate pattern analysis to EEG data to investigate how perceptual redundancy modulates visual working memory (VWM). It found that fully redundant arrays elicited early neural activity patterns distinct from arrays with any orientation differences, suggesting a separation-based account of VWM representations.

papers.title: Visual speech enhances phoneme separability in human superior temporal gyrus.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using intracranial EEG from 12 epilepsy patients, the study found that visual speech enhances phoneme separability in the human superior temporal gyrus, improving decoding accuracy at the word and phoneme levels without affecting phonetic features, and accelerating speech processing.

papers.title: Reactive and predictive processes during unpredictable driving collisions in virtual reality: an exploratory immersive study with multimodal neurophysiological monitoring
papers.summary: Used a wearable dry-electrode EEG and photoplethysmography headset in virtual reality to test whether neural activity differentiates unpredictable collision from no-collision events in 16 participants across 120 trials. Post-stimulus clusters differentiated conditions with up to 93.8% cross-validated decoding accuracy, whereas pre-stimulus time-domain discrimination was at chance; a pre-stimulus broadband spectral difference survived correction but is exploratory and requires replication.

papers.title: Multimodal Ganzfeld-induced visual experiences are associated with accompanying mental experiences and distinct EEG microstate dynamics
papers.summary: This study combined experience sampling with EEG during multimodal Ganzfeld to examine visual experiences and thought processes. Visual complexity was related to perceptual belief, prediction mismatch, updating, and prior mentation, and was accompanied by distinct nonlinear dynamics of large-scale brain networks, suggesting Ganzfeld as a model for hallucinatory mechanisms.

papers.title: Evaluation of the Recognition Performance for Four-class Fine Hand Movement Intention under a hybrid Action Observation and Motor Imagery Task.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: This study evaluates four-class fine hand movement intention recognition using a hybrid action observation and motor imagery task, integrating SMR and SSMVEP features via confidence-weighted fusion. The fusion method achieved 80.69% average accuracy for four-class recognition, with 14 participants exceeding 90% accuracy.

papers.title: Neural Dynamics of Self-Control: Pre-Choice EEG Signals Predict Yielding to Temptation.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The study introduced a dynamometer-based task to isolate self-control from cost-benefit evaluation and recorded EEG from 26 participants. It found that pre-choice EEG signals, including enhanced late positive potential (LPP) and frontoparietal network patterns peaking at 304-348 ms, predicted yielding to temptation.

papers.title: Passive Behavioral Patterns in Symptomatic WAG/Rij Rats: Dissociation From Absence Epilepsy and Sex-Dependent Link Between Early Fear Coping and Post-Stress Freezing.
papers.summary: In WAG/Rij rats with absence epilepsy, early passive coping in an active avoidance task predicted later context-inappropriate freezing in a safe environment in females but not males, and absence epilepsy severity (SWD number/duration) did not correlate with either passive behavior or freezing. The study also found low freezing levels in the safe environment across both sexes and higher SWD counts in males.

papers.title: Toward A Whole-Brain Interface Enabled by High-Resolution Surface Electrophysiology
papers.summary: The paper presents a multi-subject functional atlas of the human central nervous system based on high-resolution surface electrophysiology from the first 70 patients implanted with a conformal thin-film neural interface across more than 100 locations, comprising >100,000 electrode deployments. Aggregated recordings revealed somatotopic organization with digit representations ordered lateral-to-medial and transitions over approximately 0.8–2.0 mm, canonical movement-related beta suppression and focal high-gamma (70–200 Hz) increases, task-modulated population dynamics across cortical, brainstem, and spinal cord regions, and supported real-time neural decoding for upper extremity neuroprosthetic control and spoken-language/facial-expression decoding.

papers.title: Tetradic Dynamics of Dyadic Sensorimotor Coordination: A Multiscale EEG Hyperscanning Study
papers.summary: This dual-brain EEG hyperscanning study examined leader-follower sensorimotor coordination in healthy adult pairs using a 2x2 design crossing Role with Mirroring versus Matching, proposing a tetradic framework for dyadic interaction. Neural analyses showed greater tonic power and phasic clusters during Matching, role-dependent anticipatory and post-response patterns, and information-theoretic signatures separating Leader-weighted predictive information from Follower-specific adaptive information, with sparse Synergy and Redundancy across specific cortical regions.

papers.title: Frequency-specific resting-state EEG modulation during eyes-closed and eyes-open transitions in female soccer players.
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG in female soccer players vs. university students showed frequency- and region-specific differences in the transition between eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions, particularly in the beta and delta bands. Alpha and theta activity mainly reflected general physiological responses without sport-specific effects, but the beta and delta differences did not survive FDR correction.

papers.title: Electroencephalography in Subjective Cognitive Decline and Mild Cognitive Impairment: Systematic Review of Biomarkers, Classification, and Prognostic Evidence.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized evidence from 20 reports on EEG biomarkers, classification models, and prognostic prediction in subjective cognitive decline (SCD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Although between-group EEG differences and preliminary model performance were encouraging, no conventional diagnostic test-accuracy study was identified and certainty of evidence was very low across all evidence bodies.

papers.title: I-GraphECG: Observability-Based Lead Selection and Interpretable Disease Prediction from the 12-Lead ECG Using a Gray-Box Graph Electrophysiology Surrogate.
papers.summary: I-GraphECG is a gray-box graph electrophysiology surrogate that encodes a 12-lead median beat into 47 equivalent electrophysiological descriptors, decodes via a constrained eight-node conduction graph, and predicts disease from descriptors rather than waveform. On a clean PTB-XL four-class subset, median beats were reconstructed at median correlation 0.91 and macro-AUROC reached approximately 0.90 versus black-box references of 0.920–0.924; myocardial infarction recall was approximately 0.49, and observability-based lead selection showed every optimal three-lead set retained one precordial lead (V2–V5) and the conventional reduced set was never observability-optimal across seven noise models, with reconstruction and observability analysis transferring zero-shot to US and Chinese cohorts.

papers.title: Exploratory EEG Feature Profiles During Viewing of Six Combined Indoor Spatial-Color Conditions.
papers.summary: This exploratory study developed an EEG workflow to describe neural feature profiles during viewing of six combined indoor spatial-color conditions in 20 adults who completed three repeated counterbalanced virtual-walkthrough runs with 32-channel EEG. Of 720 planned event positions, 691 clean event-locked epochs were obtained (97.9% of epochable events), and features included ERP window amplitudes, sustained theta/alpha/beta relative power, early/middle/late power summaries, and Hilbert power-change/phase-consistency measures; the paper reports only descriptive condition-level profiles without inferential results or causal design prescriptions.

papers.title: Kv3.1 activation suppresses provoked and spontaneous seizures in a mouse Dravet syndrome model.
papers.summary: In a Scn1a haploinsufficient mouse model of Dravet syndrome and wild-type mice, repeated seizures reduced cortical Kv3.1 protein and mislocalized it in parvalbumin-positive interneurons; the Kv3.1-positive allosteric modulator AUT1 attenuated chemoconvulsant, hyperthermia-induced, and spontaneous seizures.

papers.title: Anterior temporal lobes show route-dependent sensitivity to conceptual specificity: Evidence from MEG and EEG
papers.summary: Concurrent MEG-EEG was recorded from 36 participants reading 100 conceptual triads varying parametrically in specificity, from general words (bird) to adjective-noun phrases (nocturnal bird) to specific words (owl). Bilateral anterior temporal lobes showed a non-linear pattern at 400–520 ms, with high-specificity concepts eliciting greater activity than both low-specificity words and mid-specificity phrases, and bilateral inferior frontal cortex showed a similar effect at 430–630 ms; N400 amplitude and ATL source activity dissociated in sensitivity to word frequency, suggesting high-specificity access requires individuating stored representations among competitors whereas phrases construct meaning through a different route.

papers.title: Neurotrauma During Military Training: Results of the INVestigating traIning assoCiated blasT pAthology (INVICTA) Study.
papers.summary: The five-year INVICTA study prospectively assessed 224 participants, including 104 special operators firing live rounds in heavy weapons training (HWT), 47 training controls, 36 active duty controls, and 37 instructors, with serial assessments from baseline through up to 18 months. Exposed special operators showed significant alterations in short-term memory, EEG signal complexity, and blood biomarkers tau and UCH-L1 within minutes after HWT, with gait and oculomotor changes within hours, more than 20% having at least one significant hearing threshold change, and instructors with repeated exposure over two-year tours showing greater magnitude and duration of memory and gait alterations toward the end of those tours.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
